sources.entry: DbGate - Database manager for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, SQLite and others. Runs under Windows, Linux, Mac or as web application.

summary.one_liner: DbGate is a cross-platform (no)SQL database manager that connects to many SQL and NoSQL databases from a desktop app, a web browser, or Docker.
summary.what_it_does: DbGate lets you browse and edit table data with filters, change table schema and indexes, and compare and synchronize database structures. It includes a SQL editor with formatting and code completion, a visual query designer, and an ER diagram. For MongoDB and Redis it provides a JavaScript/Redis script editor and tree views. Data can be imported and exported to CSV, Excel, JSON, NDJSON, XML and DBF, and results can be charted. The README also describes an NDJSON file viewer/editor, an AI-powered database chat, and a plugin architecture. Some supported databases and APIs are marked Premium.
use_cases: query and edit data across several databases at once
visually build SQL queries without writing SQL
export or import data between CSV, Excel, JSON and databases
explore MongoDB collections and Redis keys
browse a database from a web browser via Docker
notable: Supports both SQL databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, DuckDB and more) and NoSQL databases (MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse)
Runs as a desktop app on Windows, Linux and Mac, or as a web app in a Docker container
Foreign-key-based browsing: master/detail views, expandable columns and form view
Standalone NPM packages let scripts run without the app, e.g. CSV export
caveats: Many databases and APIs (Redshift, Cosmos DB, DynamoDB, GraphQL, OpenAPI and others) are listed as Premium features
Development setup requires several concurrent terminals and Docker for integration tests
Mobile web support is described as planned, not available
